# Intake brief — Grand Opening provides bonus for each synergy business (MS-0MV8KSPFK006HTXG)

## Headline

Grand Opening Sale currently pays a fixed bonus per **Commerce** business; it should pay per business sharing the synergy of the business opened (placed) on that same turn, so the reward tracks the player's placement rather than a hard-coded sector.

## Problem statement

`evt-grand-opening` (Grand Opening Sale, cost 300, Investment) is defined in `card-data.csv` as a `SpecificSynergy` event with a static `targetSynergy: Commerce` and `coinDelta: 450` — i.e. it always rewards `450 × (Commerce businesses on the grid)` (CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB added a same-turn placement gate requiring a business/community-space to be placed that turn). The fixed Commerce target makes the card's payoff unrelated to what the player actually opened: a player who places a non-Commerce business still gets rewarded solely for their Commerce holdings.

## Users / user stories

- **Player** — "As a player who just opened a Café (Food) next to my Bakery, I want Grand Opening Sale to pay off my Food businesses, because I built around that placement."
- **AI opponent (competitive)** — "As the AI, I want event-value estimates to match the actual dynamic payout so I don't over- or under-value Grand Opening Sale."

## Desired change

- On resolution, Grand Opening Sale's bonus applies to **each grid business/community-space sharing the synergy of the card placed (opened) this turn** — the placement that armed the gate — instead of the static `Commerce` target.
- The placement paths must record the placed card's synergy type(s) for the turn; the state machinery (week-start reset, serialisation/backfill, undo snapshot) must carry it.
- Both single-player and competitive resolution, plus AI/projection value paths and animation attribution, must use the same dynamic synergy so projections and payouts never diverge.
- Card copy/docs updated so the effect text no longer claims "from a Commerce promotion".

## Acceptance Criteria (measurable)

1. Play `evt-grand-opening` in a turn where a non-Commerce business (e.g. Food) was placed: coins increase by `450 × (number of grid cards sharing that placed business's synergy)`, and Commerce businesses are **not** counted unless they also share the placed synergy.
2. Placing a card with multiple synergy types (e.g. `Food|Culture`) rewards any grid card sharing **any** of the placed card's synergy types (union semantics, consistent with existing `synergyTypes.some()` matching).
3. Placing a community space (which already arms the gate, per the same-turn gate test) drives the synergy selection symmetrically with business placements.
4. Single-player (`resolveEvent`) and competitive (`applyCompetitiveEventEffects` / `computeOwnerEventDeltas`), the AI/projection helpers (`projectEventCoinDelta`, `computeCompetitiveEventValue`), and per-slot animation attribution (`MainStreetAdjacencyScoring`) all resolve the same dynamic synergy for the event — no divergence between projection and payout.
5. State lifecycle: the recorded placed synergy resets at week start, survives save/load with legacy backfill, and is included in the undo snapshot so undoing a placement restores the pre-placement synergy.
6. Card copy and docs updated: `card-data.csv` `effect` text, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, and `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` no longer describe a fixed Commerce promotion.
7. Tests: new/extended unit coverage for dynamic synergy resolution (single-player and competitive), union matching, community-space placements, lifecycle (reset/backfill/undo), and AI/competitive projection parity. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Do not remove or relax the existing same-turn placement gate (CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB) — this item extends its payoff semantics only.
- Keep the card's static `targetSynergy: Commerce` in `card-data.csv` **unless** the implementer can verify that removing it does not degrade market-refill relevance (`isMarketCardRelevant`) and tooltip consumers; minimal-change default is a resolution-time override keyed on `evt-grand-opening`.
- Integer-only payouts (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6): `450 × count` stays integer by construction.
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv` row 46: `event,evt-grand-opening,...,SpecificSynergy,Commerce,450,...` effect "+450 coins from a Commerce promotion."
- `businessPlacedThisTurn?: boolean` gate field: `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` (~529–534), armed in `purchaseBusiness` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` ~362), `playBusinessFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketHand.ts` ~148), `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (`MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` ~770), reset at week start (`MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` ~57), serialised/backfilled (`MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` ~359), undo-snapshotted (`MainStreetCommands.ts`).
- Resolution: `SpecificSynergy` counts `streetGrid` cards whose `synergyTypes` include `event.targetSynergy` in `resolveEvent` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` ~100), `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (~301), `computeOwnerEventDeltas` (~477); AI/competitive projections in `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` `projectEventCoinDelta` (~140) and `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` `computeCompetitiveEventValue` (~2210); per-slot animation attribution in `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` (~972).
- Tests: `tests/main-street/grand-opening-same-turn-gate.test.ts` (gate lifecycle), `tests/main-street/event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/piggyback-eligibility.test.ts` (lists `evt-grand-opening` as piggybackable).

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new state field recording the placed card's synergy types this turn (e.g. `placedBusinessSynergiesThisTurn?: SynergyType[]`), adjacent to `businessPlacedThisTurn`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` / `src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — set the new field in each of the three placement paths.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the new field alongside `businessPlacedThisTurn`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — serialise, legacy backfill, and undo snapshot for the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — dynamic synergy resolution in `resolveEvent`, `applyCompetitiveEventEffects`, `computeOwnerEventDeltas`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` / `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — mirror dynamic resolution in `projectEventCoinDelta` / `computeCompetitiveEventValue` (and check `scoreEventAction`).
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — per-slot animation attribution uses the dynamic synergy.
- `src/card-data.csv` / `docs/game/card-catalog.md` / `docs/dev/analysis/community-space-event-repricing.md` — effect copy + documentation.
- `tests/main-street/grand-opening-dynamic-synergy.test.ts` (new) + updates to `grand-opening-same-turn-gate.test.ts` and `event-card-tooltip-info.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Divergence risk**: the payout path (`resolveEvent` / competitive per-owner math) and the AI/projection paths (`projectEventCoinDelta`, `computeCompetitiveEventValue`, piggyback projection, animation attribution) share the `targetSynergy` lookup — if only the payout path is updated, the AI will mis-value the card. Mitigation: a single shared dynamic-synergy resolver used by every path; AC 4 + projection-parity tests.
- **Piggyback interplay** (competitive, `evt-grand-opening` is piggybackable): piggyback reward projections must reflect the dynamic payout too — include in AC 4/7 coverage.
- **Scope-creep risk**: predictive/strategy re-tuning of Grand Opening's cost/coinDelta in light of the dynamic target is **out of scope** here; record any rebalancing as a new linked work item.
- **Assumption**: union synergy matching for multi-synergy cards, community-space placements drive selection, most-recent placement wins — recorded in the Appendix; producer confirmation requested.

## Related work

- MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5 — Re-price community spaces and events relative to slower business payback (related balance context)
- MS-0MUX8J9KJ005ZKDW — AI uses community space cards too much (AI valuation context)
- MS-0MUWKG6NS006OG2D — Community Garden should be Entertainment (synergy data context)
- CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB — Grand Opening Sale same-turn placement gate (commit `a3e2b5de`; basis for this change)
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/completed item found.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking producer questions were required — the seed intent ("bonus for each business with the same synergy as the one opened on that turn") is specific, and the remaining decisions follow from repo mechanics and precedent. Records (idempotent; do not duplicate on re-run):

- Q: Dynamic synergy should be union or exact for multi-synergy placed cards? — **Answer (research, agent-recommended):** union — any grid card sharing any of the placed card's `synergyTypes` counts; consistent with existing `synergyTypes.some()`/`.includes()` matching in `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` and `isMarketCardRelevant`. Source: repo matching code; optional producer confirmation.
- Q: Does a community-space placement drive the synergy (it already arms the gate)? — **Answer (research, agent-recommended):** yes, symmetric with the gate (CG-0MTIOCBH400970OB test arms on "business (or community-space)"). Source: existing gate behaviour + test file.
- Q: Which placement counts if a player places multiple cards in one turn? — **Answer (research, agent-recommended):** the most recent placement (last placement wins), matching conventional "the one opened" reading; single-action turns make collisions rare. Source: default `actionsRemaining` = 1.
- Q: Should the static `targetSynergy: Commerce` row field be removed from CSV? — **Answer (research, agent-recommended):** no — keep it as the static field; override dynamically at resolution keyed on `evt-grand-opening`, to avoid silent changes to market-refill relevance (`isMarketCardRelevant`) and tooltip consumers. Source: `MainStreetStateSetup.ts` relevance logic, tooltip tests.

# Extract the storyline features — the generic storyline system in TCE core

**Headline:** Move the branching storyline mechanic from tce-main-street into Tableau-Card-Engine core as a standalone, pluggable generic system; add a Gym demo scene; refactor Main Street to consume the core system while preserving current behaviour exactly.

## Problem statement

The storyline mechanic (named, multi-step incident arcs where a drawn card offers branching options and the player's decision selects the next card) lives today in tce-main-street as Main-Street-specific modules (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` and friends). No other TCE game can reuse it, and the engine has no generic home for branching narrative. The code was deliberately built behind an "extraction seam" (MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV) in anticipation of this move; this work performs the move.

## Users (with user stories)

- **As a game developer building on TCE**, I want a standalone generic storyline engine (types, compilation, resolution, journal helpers, pluggable UI adapter) in core so any game can ship branching card narratives without copying Main Street code.
- **As a TCE core engineer**, I want a Gym demo scene that exercises the draw → decision → successor-chain loop so the mechanic is demonstrable and testable in isolation.
- **As a Main Street player**, I want the five shipped storylines to keep behaving exactly as they do today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Standalone generic storyline system in core** — a new core module (no Main-Street imports) exposes:
   - the generic types (`StorylineOption`, `CompiledStoryline`, pending-choice state) and the legacy `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` → option-list compilation, CSV `options` encoding parsing, and the registered-option registry at parity with today's `MainStreetStoryline.ts` behaviour;
   - resolution semantics exactly preserved: `apply`/`skip` effect policy, successor precedence (resolver → seeded candidate draw → legacy id), one `state.rng()` draw per candidate selection at resolution time (replay-safe; terminal options consume no draw), chain-card push with deterministic serial naming;
   - a **pluggable UI seam**: core defines a storyline UI/overlay adapter interface (names, choice-dialog labels, story-update lines, journal) with a default implementation; games supply their own presentation without touching core logic. Core must not depend on Phaser or Main-Street internals.
   - Unit tests in core proving parity with the current model tests (compile, options parsing, condition filtering, RNG semantics).

2. **Gym demo scene** — a new scene `GymStorylineScene` in `core/example-games/gym` (registered in the Gym router) where a small hand of story cards deals a branching narrative: the player draws a card, sees the options, picks one, and the choice determines the next card; chain ends cleanly. Pure logic is exercised by a unit test; the scene runs in the Gym smoke test.

3. **Main Street refactored to consume core** — the URL/local exports of `MainStreetStoryline.ts`, `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` and `MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` are re-implemented as thin adapters over the core module (the seam's intended design); the exported API surface used by callers stays backward-compatible. Existing storyline tests in tce-main-street pass unchanged: `storyline-model`, `storyline-csv-options`, `storyline-regression-harness`, `storyline-player-agency`, `storyline-journal`, `storyline-author`, `storyline-graph`, `storyline-graph-svg`, `MainStreetEventChoiceUndo`, `validate-storylines` and the doc-drift test.

4. **Behaviour preserved** — the five shipped storylines (tax, health, economy, labour, restaurant) and the CSV/card-pack authoring formats are unaffected; CSV `options` encodings authored for Main Street remain valid; RNG seed replays produce identical results.

5. **Documentation** — `docs/game/storylines.md` (Main-Street view) and a new/updated core dev reference documenting the generic module, the pluggable UI adapter and the Gym demo are kept current and covered by the doc-drift guard.

6. **Full test suite passes** — `npm test` in core (incl. smoke) and `npm test` in tce-main-street both green.

## Constraints

- **API parity:** the types and function signatures consumers rely on today must not change in a breaking way; the seam is the contract.
- **Determinism/replay:** RNG consumption (one seeded draw per candidate selection) must be byte-for-byte preserved.
- **Legacy equivalence:** legacy two-way choice cards compile to exactly the same two options as today.
- **Pluggable UI:** the UI seam must be an interface; core ships a default, games override. No Phaser dependency in the generic module.
- **Repo boundaries:** extraction lands in the `core` submodule (Tableau-Card-Engine). Main Street imports it via the existing `@core-*` alias mechanism.

## Existing state

- The storyline mechanic is implemented in tce-main-street: `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` (compilation + registry + resolution + pending-choice lifecycle, already documented as an extraction seam), `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` (journal + choice-clarity helpers), `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` (player-agency helpers), plus types in `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` and engine integration in `src/MainStreetEngine*`/`src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`.
- Five shipped storylines, CSV `options` encoding, a storyline graph/manifest toolchain, and an extensive test suite.
- The tce-main-street repo already consumes core via aliases (`@core-engine`, `@card-system`, …) and `vite.config.ts` resolves the sibling `./core` checkout (a git submodule).

## Desired change

- Create a new core module (e.g. `core/src/story-line/` — name TBD at implementation) containing types, compilation, resolution, journal/pure helpers and the pluggable UI adapter interface, mirroring today's behaviour.
- Ship a Gym demo scene exercising the mechanic.
- Refactor tce-main-street storyline modules to delegate to the core module, keeping behaviour identical.

## Key Files:

- `core/src/story-line/…` — new generic module (types, compile, resolve, journal, ui-adapter).
- `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts` — new demo scene (+ Gym router registration).
- `core/tests/…` — new unit tests for the story-line module + gym scene.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` — refactored to consume core.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — types re-exported from core (or kept in sync) for backward compatibility.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — updated; new core dev reference for the story-line module.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** gym scene stays a proof-of-concept demo (user-confirmed); storyline *authoring editor*, *conditional/cost-gated options* (MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9) and card-pack *manifest export* are out of scope and tracked by their own work items.
- **Submodule coupling:** changes land in the `core` submodule first; tce-main-street tests only see them after the submodule is bumped — coordinate commit order (core first, then Main Street submodule pointer + refactor).
- **Behaviour drift:** risk that refactoring changes subtle semantics (RNG order, option-order, message text). Mitigation: parity tests in core + unchanged Main Street suite as the gate; review transcript strings carefully (story-update text) since those are asserted by tests.
- **Assumption:** the exported names of the three Main-Street modules remain callable as today (adapter layer), even if their bodies delegate to core.
- **Assumption:** journal/choice-clarity UI logic moves to core as pure helpers behind the UI adapter; the Main-Street overlay presentation stays game-side.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV** — *Storyline model & extraction seam* (completed): laid the seam this work formalises.
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — *write storylines* (completed): parent epic that produced the mechanic.
- **MS-0MV8KQJR30007JL5** — multi-way options / CSV `options` encoding (completed): formats that must stay valid.
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** — *Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects* (open): future extension on top of the generic system.
- **MS-0MUSY1K6B00095AT** — *Storyline editor test harness & fixtures* (open): related editor tooling, out of scope.
- **MS-0MV8KQQQ90044CM5** — *Migrate five shipped storylines* (completed): the five arcs that must keep behaving as now.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Scope of A (extraction): what parts move to core vs stay game-specific? (model/resolution → core? journal overlay UI → core? graph tools → core?)"
  Answer (rgardler, interactive reply): "Your call. We are aiming for a generic storyline system in core. It needs to be standalone so that we can build the Gym scene as a demo. Key components need to be pluggable, such as the UI."
  Research: `MainStreetStoryline.ts` is already documented as the extraction seam with migration notes; `MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`/`MainStreetStorylineUi.ts` are pure Phaser-free helpers — portable to core behind a UI adapter. Graph/manifest tooling stays with Main Street docs/tooling (no core dependency observed). Key files: `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts`.
- Q: "Scope of B (gym scene): proof-of-concept demo showcasing the mechanic, or something more elaborate?"
  Answer (rgardler, interactive reply): "A" — a proof-of-concept/demo scene in the core Gym.
  Research: `core/example-games/gym/scenes/` holds per-mechanic demo scenes (e.g. `GymDeckRngScene`, `GymHandPileScene`) registered in `GymRegistry.ts`; a `GymStorylineScene` follows the same pattern.
- Q: "Existing storylines: must Main Street be refactored (not removed) to consume the core engine storyline system?"
  Answer (rgardler, interactive reply): "yes" — core provides the engine, Main Street becomes a consumer, behaviour unchanged.
  Research: Main Street already imports core via `@core-*` aliases resolved by `vite.config.ts`; the seam module was designed for exactly this delegation.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV16VY0U0024E4T** – Production residential pack content & builder wrapper (completed)
- **MS-0MTRRYOT6001167R** – Change the name of Physiotherapy business card to Physiotherapist (completed)
- **MS-0MUSY1UIR007XLOQ** – Editor documentation & final regression (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: add, branching, card, cards, comes (+35 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: add, card, cards, comes, continue (+34 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, card, cards, comes, continue (+34 more)
